39.  Advertisement  Of  films. — Any  person  advertising  a film  certified  for 
public  exhibition  restricted  to  adults  or  the  exhibition  of  such  film  by  means 
of  insertions  in  newspapers,  hoardings,  posters,  or  handbills  shall,  after 
the  date  of  its  certification,  indicate  in  such  insertions  in  newspapers, 
hoardings,  posters  or  handbills  that  the  film  has  been  certified  for  public 
exhibition  restricted  to  adults  only. 


40.  Maintenance  Of  Register. — (1)  The  Hoard  shall  maintain  a register 
in  which  shall  be  entered  — 

(a)  tin1  name  of  every  film  examined  under  the  Act; 

(h)  the  name  of  the  person  applying  for  a certificate; 

(<;)  the  name  of  the  person  or  company  producing  or  releasing  the  film; 

(d  ) the  name  of  t lit'  country  in  which  the  film  was  originally  produced; 

(e)  the  name  of  the  place  where  the  film  was  examined; 

(f)  the  date  of  the  examination; 

(g)  the  names  of  the  persons  who  examined  the  film; 

(h)  the  result  of  the  examination  and  of  any  further  proceedings 

thereon ; 

(i)  the  number  and  date  of  the  certificate'  issued,  if  any,  together  with 

a copy  of  any  endorsement  made  thereon. 

(2)  Eor  tlie  purpose  of  enabling  flu*  Hoard  to  maintain  such  a register, 
file  Regional  Officers  at  Honibny.  Calcutta  and  Madras  shall  each  maintain 
similar  registers  in  respect  of  applications  for  certification  made  to  them  and 
send  to  the  Hoard  a duplicate  copy  of  every  entry  made  in  it,  as  soon  as  may 
he,  after  it  has  been  made. 

(3)  A copy  of  tlie  entries  in  tin*  register  maintained  bv  the  Hoard  made 
luring  any  month  shall  be  sent  to  the  Regional  Officers  at  Honiba.v,  ( ab  utta 
and  Madras  during  the  next  following  month. 


41.  Certain  films  to  continue  to  remain  uncertified  films. — If  a film  has 
been  declared  by  a notification  issued  before  the  loth  January,  1951,  by 
a n x State  Government  to  be  an  uncertified  film  in  any  part  or  parts  ni  the 
State  concerned  and  if  the  said  notification  lias  not  ceased  to  be  in  force  by

( ( ’ensor, ship ) Rules,  J95I,  the  film  shall  not  be  publicly  exhibited  unless  it 
is  certified  tor  public  exhibition  in  accordance  with  the  provisions  of  these 
rules  • 

Provided  that  before  certifying  any  such  film  for  public  exhibition  the 
Hoard  shall  obtain  the  prior  approval  of  the  Central  Government. 


42.  Repeal. — The  Cinematograph  (Censorship)  Rules,  1951,  are  hereby 
repealed.

MINISTRY  OF  IRRIGATION  AND  POWER 

New  Delhi,  the  18th  October  1958/Asvina  1880  (Saka). 

RESOLUTION 

No.  DW.V.  5X6(6)/ 58/1. — The  Government  of  India  have  accepted  the 
recommendations  contained  in  volume  T of  the  report  of  the  Ilijjh  LeveL 
Committee  on  floods  regarding  the  functions  of  the  Central  Flood  Coptrol 
Hoard  set  up  under  the  Government  of  India,  Ministry  of  Irrigation  and 
Power,  Resolution  No.  DW . V.  14(7)  / 54,  dated  the  8th  September  1954,  as 
amended  from  time  to  time,  and  have  accordingly  decided  that  the  func- 
tions of  the  said  Board  shall  hereafter  be  as  follows:  — 

^i)  to  lay  down  the  general  principles  and  policies  in  connection  with 
floods  and  flood  control  measures ; 

(ii)  to  consider  and  approve  the  master  plans  for  flood  control  as  sub- 
mitted by  the  States  or  River  Commissions ; 

(iii)  to  consider  and  approve  specific  schemes  of  flood  control  works  sub- 

mitted to  them  for  approval  ; and 

(iv)  to  arrange  for  necessary  assistance  in  connection  with  investiga- 

tions, planning  and  execution  of  flood  control  works. 

T.  SIVASANKAR,  Secy. 


ORDER 

OrdesDd  that  this  resolution  be  communicated  to  all  State  Governments, 
all  the  Ministries  of  Government  of  India,  Prime  Minster's  Secretariat*  the 
Private  and  Military  Secretaries  to  the.  iFresident,  the  Cabinet  Secretariat, 
the  Department  of  Parliamentary  Affairs,  the  Rajya  Sabha  Secretariat, 
the  Dok  Sabha  Secretariat,  the  Planning  Commission  and  the  Comptroller 
and  Auditor-General  of  India. 

Ordered  also  that  the  resolution  be  published  in  the  Gazette  of  India 
and  that  the  State  Government  be  requested  to  publish  it  i»n  the  State  Gazettes 
for  general  information. 

T.  SIVASANKAR,  S*cy.

New  Delhi,  the  18th  October  1958/Asvina  26th,  1880(Saka) 

RESOLUTION 

No.  DW. V. 510(6) / 58-11. — The  Government  of  India  have  accepted  the 
i eronnnemlat  ions  contained  in  Volume  J of  the  report  of  the  High  Level 
Committee  on  Floods  regarding  the  functions  of  the  four  River  Commissions 
(Floods)  set  up  under  the  Government  of  India,  Ministry  of  Irrigation  and 
Power,  Resolution  No.  DW. V.  1 4(9 > /54,  dated  the  30th  September  1954, 
Resolution  No.  DW. V.14(9) /54-(  1 ) , dated  the  31st  January  1965,  and 
Resolution  No.  DW.V.  14(42) /55,  dated  the  30th  November  1955.  as  amended 
from  time  to  time  and  have  accordingly  decided  that  the  functions  of  the 
said  Commissions  shall  hereafter  he  as  follows:  — 

(1)  To  examine  ami  recommend  for  approval  to  the  Central  Flood 

Control  Board,  outline  master  plans  for  flood  control  works  of 
the  river  basin  concerned  as  prepared  by  the  States; 

(2)  to  advise  the  State  Governments  on  technical  problems  pertaining 

to  flood  control  whenever  referred  to  them ; and 

(3)  to  advise  the  Central  Flood  Control  Board  i>n  respect  of 

flood  problems  on  which  there  is  difference  of  technical  opinion 
between  two  or  more  States,  or  between  the  Central  Water  and 
Power  Commission  and  the  State  authorities. 

T.  SIVASANKAR,  Secy.

Provisions  like  section  7(d)  have  been  a familiar  feature  of  election  laws 
from  very  early  times.  They  are  based  on  a sound,  solemn  and  salulor.v 
principle  which  democracies  or  democratic  constitutions  can  ill  afford  to 
span*  or  ignore.  Their  purpose  is  to  guarantee  flu*  purity  of  the  legislature 
and  of  flu*  administrative  machinery  as  well  and  it  has  been  variously  pm 
bs  various  eminent  judges  and  noted  authorities  but  always  with  an  eve 
to  flu*  grantee  of  puritx  of  flu*  legislature  ami  admiuist  rat  ion  and  fo  keep 
flu*  sourer  or  the  fountain  bead  of  Ia\s  and  flu*  sf  ream  of  admiuist  rat  ion 
unsullied  and  free  from  corrupt  ion.  The  basic  standpoint  is  “to  prevent 
conflict  between  interest  and  duty  which  would  otherwise  inevitably  arise” 
j per  liindlay  b..l.  in  Nortf  on  vs.  Wilson  (1889)  2”.  Q.E.1>.  744  at  p.  748] 
and  to  prevent  the  member  concerned  from  being-  exposed  to  temptation  or 
even  flu*  semblance  of  temptation  [per  Lord  Graham  M.R.  in  the  same  case 
Norffon  vs.  Willson  (1889)  Q.H.l).  744  at  p.  717]  and  that  has  never 

been  questioned.  It  has  also  been  authoritatively  laid  down  that  “a 
concealed  interest  is  as  much  as  interest  as  an  open  interest,  and  the  court 
in  such  matters  will  always  look  at  the  substance  and  not  at  flu*  colourable 
exterior”  | per  Me.Pardie.  J in  Evereth  vs.  Griffiths  (19^4)  l.K.ll.  941  at 
p.  947].  If  has  been  ruled  further  that  “no  device  to  conceal  the  real  nature 
ot  the  transaction  would  prevail”  [per  Eord  Loveturn  E.(\  in  North  vs. 
Taylor  (190(>)  A.G.  878  at  p.  88(1].  In  that  context,  flu*  word  “interest” 
in  section  7(d)  may  well  receive  a with*  connotation  and  max  well  include 
e\en  more  than  material  interest  but,  for  reasons  which  it  is  not  necessary 
In  examine  now.  decisions  have  restricted  it  to  pecuniary  or  at  flu*  most 
material  interest  and  that,  as  we  shall  presently  see,  being-  sufficient  for 
mu  present  purpose,  any  further  discussion  on  the  point,  of  construction  is 
unnecessary.

it  is  admittedly  a letter  paper  of  the  said  concern  aud,  in  the  absence  of  any 
explanation  or*  denial  from  Roy  in  the  witness  box,  it  may  safely  be  taken 
that  “our  business”  had  reference  to  the  said  concern.  Even  if  the 
7>urticular  letter  paper  had  been  signed  in  blauk  like  other  similar  letters 
or  papers  and  the  body  of  the  letter  [Ext.  19(4)]  had  been  manufactured 
thereon  as  suggested  by  the  appelants  it  is  difficult  to  dismiss  it  from 
consideration  as  it  is  inadmissible  that  Roy  would  have  so  signed  it,  and  lie 
not  been  intimately  connected  with  the  concern  Indo  German  Trade  Centre 
either  as  proprietor  or  having  a share  or  interest — to  wit,  material  interest-- 
therein.  This  letter  [Ext.  19(4)]  is  therefore  a very  significant  document 
and  is  sufficient  in  our  opinion,  in  the  facts  of  this  particular  case  and  in 
the  context  of  Roy’s  absence  from  the  evidence  above  to  prove  Roy’s  material 
interest  in  the  concern  Indo  German  Trade  Centre  and  so  in  the  two 
contracts  under  consideration. 

The  cheque,  Ext.  Hi,  again  along  with  the  Buuk  papers  Exts.  23,  23(1) 
and  29  also  support  the  above  position.  They  show  and  that  is  not  disputed 
that  on  or  about  20th  October  1955  appellant  Biren  Roy  received  a sum  of 
Its.  1,190  from  Indo  German  Trade  Centre.  P.W.  10  K.  C.  Ghosh  Las 
deposed  that  the  above  payment  was  made  to  Roy  as  proprietor  of  Indo- 
Gerinan  Trade  Centre  on  account  of  the  profits  of  the  said  concern  but 
even  if  we  do  not  accept  the  said  statement,  the  payment  at  least  shows 
that  Roy  had  some  financial  connection  with  the  said  firm.  Roy  has  not 
deposed  to  explain  the  above  payment  and  the  only  attempt  that  lias  been 
made  by  the  appellants  in  that  behalf  is  the  production  of  the  audited 
balance-sheet  of  the  firm  of  an  earlier  year,  namely,  1954  and  to  argue 
therefrom  that  Roy  was  a mere,  to  wit,  an  ordinary  creditor  of  the  firm 
and  had  a loan  account,  as  shown  in  the  said  balance-sheet,  presumably  as 
such  creditor.  We  are,  however,  wholly  unconvinced  by  that  argument  mil 
attempted  explanation  on  the  part  of  the  appellants,  particularly  in  the 
absence  of  Roy  and  also  of  B.  K.  Mukherjee  from  the  witness  box,  and 
the  paper  (Ext.  E)  produced  by  the  appellants  for  the  above  purpose,  is  in 
our  opinion,  wholly  insufficient  to  support  the  said  explanation.  Indeed.  It 
seems  to  us  that  hud  the  appellant's  said  explanation  been  true,  other  ami 
much  better  materials  could  and  would  have  been  produced  by  them.  In 
this  context  and  in  the  present  state  of  the  record,  we  are  inclined  to  think 
that  Roy  had  sufficient  financial  interest  in  the  firm  or  business  of  Indo- 
German  Trade  Centre  and  was  at  least  the  financier,  if  not  the  proprietor 
of  the  said  firm,  namely,  Indo-German  Trade  Centre,  and  that 
would  certainly  give  him  a material  interest  in  the  said  firm  and  in  its 
aforesaid  contracts,  sufficient  to  bring  him  within  the  mischief  of 
section  7(d). 

It  appears  further  from  the  compromise  decree  (Ext.  21)  that  Roy  was 
the  teuant  iu  occupation  of  Room  No.  28,  Stephen  House  (where  tne 
Indo-German  Trade  Centre  had  its  office)  up  to  1955  and  undertook  the 
liability  for  rent  up  to  March,  1955  and  also  for  damages  for  use  and 
occupation  for  April  and  May  of  that  year.  It  appears  also  from  the 
balance-sheet.  Ext.  E,  that  the  Indo-German  Trade  Centre  was  not  paying 
the  rent,  the  appellants  not  having  contended  that  the  said  firm’s  liability 
under  the  loan  account  of  Roy  was  for  rent  of  its  said  business  premises. 
It  follows,  therefore,  that  Roy  was  paying  the  rent,  etc.,  for  the  Indo-German 
Trade  Centre’s  business  premises  and  he  was,  therefore,  at  least  materially 
interested  in  its  contract  or  contracts  even  if  he  was  not  its  proprietor  nor 
had  any  share  or  other  pecuniary  or  financial  interest  therein — within  rhe 
meaning  of  section  7(d)  [vide  in  this  connection  (1920)  2.  K.B.  636]. 

In  the  above  context  the  letter  (Ext.  3)  also  may  be  read  to  support 
above  conclusion.  We  are  just  incidentally  referring  to  the  said  letter  as 
even  without  that,  the  conclusion  in  view  of  our  foregoing  discussion  would 
be  the  same.  In  that  ^ view,  it  is  not  strictly  necessary  to  consider  the 
question  of  privilege  raised  in  connection  with  the  said  letter  (Ext.  3)  but 
as  the  said  question  has  been  fully  argued  before  us,  we  proceed  to  express 
briefly  our  views  on  the  same.  Privilege  has  been  claimed  by  the  head  of 
the  department  which  had  produced  rhe  letter  on  spbpoeaa  from  the  , 
Tribunal.  The  claim  has  been  made  by  a purported  affidavit  which,  however.

Calcutta,  the  22nd  December  1958. 

The  Examination  of  candidates  for  Mukhtarship 
in  mofussil  courts  subordinate  to  the  High 
Court  at  Calcutta.

will  be  bold  on  the  25 tb  and  2(>tli  of  February  1959,

University  of  Calcutta. 

One  Paper  will  be  set  each  day  for  Mukhtarship 
Examination  from  J2  noon  to  3 p.m.,  on  the  25th 
and  2bth  of  February  1959. 

In  no  circumstances,  any  candidate  be  admitted 
to  the  Examination  after  these  hours. 

The  candidates  will  be  required  to  produce  at 
tile  Examination  Hull,  the  Extracts  from  the

Examination  Hall  with  any  memoranda  or  loose 


paper  of  any  description  (with  exception  of  the 
said  Extract).

exception  of  pens  which  the  candidates  must 
bring  with  them.

Tlu  Bengal  Engineering  College  will  open  next  session  on  July  (I.  IBM). 
The  College,  which  is  completely  residential,  prepares  students'  for  the 
RE.  llegree  Examination  of  the  Calcutta  Cnivei.-ity  in  Civil,  Mechanical,

rn  tlu*  results  of  an  Admission  Test  consisting*  of  a written  examination  for

in  ay  be  obtained  from  the  College  Office  either  personally  or  by  sending*  an

BENGAL  ENGINEERING  COLLEGE

The  Bengal  Engineering-  College  will  open  next  session  on  July  6,  1959. 
The  College,  which  is  completely  residential,  prepares  students  for  the 
B.E.  Degree  Examination  of  the  Calcutta  University  in  Civil,  Mechanical, 
Electrical,  Metallurgical,  Mining  and  Tele-Communication  Engineering, 
and  for  the  Degree  in  Architecture  Arch.).  Admission  will  be  granted 
cn  the  results  of  an  Admission  Test  consisting  of  a written  examination  Cor 
all  landidutes,  to  be  held  on  April  27  and  28,  1959  (and  also  on  April  29 
for  Arrhitectme  candidates!,  a Viva  Voce  and  an  Aptitude  Test,  and  a

made  in  the  prescribed  form.  Tin-  prospectus  and  the  application  form 
may  be  obtained  from  the  College  Office  either  personally  or  by  sending  an 
Tj  natfimped  Sclf-tuld-ressed  envelope*  of  ioolscape  size.  A number  of  scholar-

of  the  Admission  Test.  Applications  will  be  entertained  from  candidates 
who  have  either  previously  passed  the  l.Se.  Examination  or  have  appeared 
in  that  examination  this  year  with  Physics,  Chemistry  and  Mathematics.

BENGAL  ENGINEERING  COLLEGE 
P.O.  Botanic  Garden,  Howrah 

Tile  Bengal  Engineering  College  will  open  next  session  on  July  6,  1959. 
The  College,  which  is  completely  residential,  prepares  students  for  the 
B.E.  Degree  Examination  of  the"  Calcutta  University  in  Civil,  Mechanical, 
Electrical,  Metallurgical,  Mining  and  Tele-Communication  Engineering, 
and  for  the  Degree  m Architecture.  (B.  Arch.).  Admission  will  be  granted 
cn  the  results  of  an  Admission  Test  consisting  of  a written  examination  for 
all  candidates,  to  he  held  on  April  27  and  28,  1959  (and  also  on  April  29 
for  Architecture  candidates),  a Viva  Voce  and  an  Aptitude  Test,  and  a 
medical  examination,  commencing  on  May  18,  1959.  Applications  must  bo 
made  in  the  jiresn  ■ lied  foim.  The  prospectus  aud  the  application  form 
may  be  obtained  from  the  College  Oflice  either  personally  or  by  sending  an 
Unstamped  Self -add  rested  envelope  of  fool  scape  size.  A number  of  scholar- 
ships and  stipends  will  be  awarded  to  meritorious  students  on  the  results 
of  the  Admission  Test.  Applications  will  be  entertained  from  candidates 
who  have  either  previously  passed  the  I. Sc.  Examination  or  have  appeared 
in  that  examination  this  year  with  Physics,  Chemistry  and  Mathematics. 
The  selection  of  the  latter  category  of  candidates  will,  however,  be  subject 
to  their  passing  the  examination  this  year.  Candidates  must  not  be  over 
20  years  of  age  on  January  1,  1959,  but  the  age  limit  may  be  relaxed  uj>  to 
22  years  with  the  prior  approval  of  Government  in  the  case  of  deserving 
applicants  belonging  to  the  educationally  backward  classes  and  communities. 
A total  of  fifteen  candidates  may  be  admitted  from  the  States  in  which 
there  are  no  engineering  colleges.  These  candidates  will  not  be  nominated 
as  in  previous  years,  but  will  have  to  apply  to  the  Principal  and  appear  for 
examination  and  interview  in  the  ordinary  way.  Separate  centres  may  be 
opened  in  the  States,  where  there  are  no  engineering  colleges  provided 
there  is  sufficient  number  of  candidates  for  these  centres,  but  Buch  candi- 
dates who  aro  successful  at  the  w’ritten  tost  will  be  required  to  appear  for 
\ iva  Voce  and  Aptitude  Test  and  medical  examination  at  the  P.E.  College. 
Application  form  which  will  be  available  from  the  College  Office  from 
March  9,  1959  onwards,  must  reach  the  College  Office  by  April  13,  1959. 


A.  C.  ROY, 

Principal,  Bengal  Engineering  College*

THE  CALCUTTA  GAZETTE,  MARCH  5,  1060 


BENGAL  ENGINEERING  COLLEGE 
P.O.  Botanic  Garden.  Howrah 

The  Bengal  Engineering  College  will  open  next  session  on  July  6,  1959 
The  College,  which  is  completely  residential,  prepares  students  for  the 
B.E.  Degree  Examination  of  the  Calcutta  University  in  Civil,  Mechanical, 
Electrical,  Metallurgical,  Mining  and  Tele-Communication  Engineering, 
and  for  the  Degree  in  Architecture  (B.  Arch.).  Admission  will  be  granted 
cn  the  results  of  an  Admission  Test  consisting  of  a written  examination  for 
all  candidates,  to  be  held  on  April  27  and  28,  1959  (and  also  on  April  29 
for  Architecture  candidates),  a Viva  Voce  and  an  Aptitude  Test,  and  a 
medical  examination,  commencing  on  May  18,  1959.  Applications  must  be 
made  in  the  prescribed  form.  The  prospectus  and  the  application  form 
may  be  obtained  from  the  College  Office  either  personally  or  by  sending  an 
Unstamped  Self-addressed  envelope;  of  foolscape  size.  A number  of  scholar- 
ships and  stipends  will  be  awarded  to  meritorious  students  on  the  results 
of  the  Admission  Test.  Applications  will  be  entertained  from  candidates 
who  have  either  previously  passed  the  I. Sc.  Examination  or  have  appeared 
in  that  examination  this  year  with  Physics,  Chemistry  and  Mathematics. 
The  selection  of  the  latter  category  of  candidates  will,  however,  be  subject 
to  their  passing  the  examination  "this  year.  Candidates  must  not  be  over 
20  years  of  age  on  January  1,  1959,  but  the  age  limit  may  be  relaxed  up  to 
22  years  with  the  prior  approval  of  Government  in  the  case  of  deserving 
applicants  belonging  to  the  educationally  backward  classes  and  communities. 
A total  of  fifteen  candidates  may  be  admitted  from  the  States  in  which 
there  are  no  engineering  colleges.  These  candidates  will  not  be  nominated 
as  in  previous  years,  but.  will  have  to  apply  to  the  Principal  and  appear  for 
examination  and  interview  in  the  ordinary  way.  Separate  centres  may  be 
opened  in  the  States,  where  there  are  no  engineering  colleges  provided 
there  is  sufficient  number  of  candidates  for  these  centres,  but  such  candi- 
dates who  are  successful  at  the  written  test  will  be  required  to  appear  for 
Viva  Voce  and  Aptitude  Test  and  medical  examination  at  the  B.E.  College. 
Application  form  which  will  be  available  from  the  College  Office  from 
March  9,  1959  onwards,  must  reach  the  College  Office  by  April  13,  1959. 

A C.  ROY, 

Principal,  Bengal  Engineering  College.

For  voltage  not  exceeding  ‘'Medium  Pressure”  (Indian

(i)  Wiring  ol  buildings  (for  lights,  fans  ami  small  motors) — 

(a)  Cleat,  wood  easing  and  capping  systems  employing 
wires  and  cables  other  than  paper  insulated  cables. 

(It)  Metal  sheathed,  tough  rubber  and  conduit  .systems 
(also  any  other  system  as  jiermitted  under  the  Indian 
Klectrieity  Act,  1910,  and  Indian  Electricity  Rules, 
1956),  using  wires  and  cables  other  than  paper 
* insulated  cables. 

(ii)  Motor  wiring  (including  generators),  in  conduit  or  load 
sheathed  with  wires  and  cables  other  than  pa} sir  insulated  cables.

EDUCATION  DIRECTORATE 

NOTIFICATION 

No.  1T.B.  — 17th  March  1959.  — It  is  hereby  notified  for  general  informa- 
tion that  the  text-books  on  the  following*  subjects  for  use  in  classes  III,  IV 
and  V of  all  schools  and  madrasahs  in  West  Bengal  written  in  accordance 
with  the  prescribed  syllabus  are  approved  for  a period  of  one  year  with  effect 
from  April  1959. 

N.Ji. — (i)  Prior  to  the  publication  of  a new  edition,  all  additions, 
alterations  or  omissions  in  the  text  of  an  approved  book  must,  receive  the 
sanction  of  the  Text-Hook  Committee.  Any  deviation  from  this  instruction 
will  render  a book  liable  to  immediate  withdrawal  from  the  list. 

(ii)  Any  deterioration  in  the  quality  of  paper,  printing  or  illustrations 
of  an  approved  hook  will  render  it  liable  to  immediate  withdrawal  from  the 
list. 

(iii)  Misleading  statements  on  the  cover  or  title  page  should  be  avoided.

No.  4T.B. — Oth  April  1959.  — It  is  hereby  notified  for  general  informa- 
tion that  tin*  text-books  on  the  following  subjects  for  use  in  classes  3 to  V 
of  all  schools  and  madrasahs  ill  \\  est  Bengal  written  in  accordance  with  the 
prescribed  syllabus  are  appioved  for  a period  of  one  \ear  with  effect  from 
April  1959. 

N.B. — (i)  Piior  to  the  publication  of  a new  edition,  all  additions, 
alterations  or  omissions  in  the  text  of  an  approved  book  must  receive  the 
sanction  of  the  Text-Book  Committee.  Any  deviation  from  this  instruction 
will  lender  a book  liable  to  immediate  withdrawal  from  the  list. 

< ii ) Any  deterioration  in  the  quality  of  paper,  pointing  or  illustrations 
of  an  approved  book  will  render  ii  liable  to  immediate  withdrawal  from  the 
list. 

(lii)  Misleading  statements  on  the  cover  or  title  page  should  be  avoided.

DIRECTORATE  OF  BOILERS,  WEST  BENGAL 

NOTICE 

Calcutta,  the  25th  May  1959. 

II  is  notified  for  general  information  that  the 
next  Proficiency  Exam  illation  of  Boiler  Engineers 
under  the  West  Bengal  Boiler  Engineers* 
Examination  Rules,  1950,  will  commence  on  and 
from  Monday,  the  20th  duly  1959.  The  intending 
candidates  must,  submit  their  applications  in  the 
prescribed  form  to  be  obtained  from  this 
Directorate  together  with  the  necessary  treasury 
chalan,  obtained  on  payment  of  the  usual  examina- 
tion fee  to  the  Chief  Inspector  of  Boilers,  West 
Bengal,  by  the  15th  June  1959.  Fee  is  to  be 
deposited  into  the  Treasury  under  the  head 
“XXX  VI — Miscellaneous  Departments — Fees  for 
Inspection  of  Steam  Boilers — Miscellaneous”. 

S.  C.  ROY, 

Chief  Inspector  of  Boilers  and  Chairman, 
Board  of  Examiners.

General  Instructions  to  candidates  applying  In  response  to 
advertisements  issued  by  the  Commission  for  recruit- 
ment to  posts  by  "Selection”. 

(1)  Instructions  regarding  submission  of  application. — 

Applications  are  to  he  made  cm  the  prescribed  torm  which 
will  be  available  from  the  office  oi  the  Public  Service 
Commission,  West  Bengal.  Anderson  House  (ground 
floor),  Alipore.  Calcutta  27.  personally  or  on  semiing  a 
large  self-addressed  envelope  with  stamps  sufficient  to 
cover  the  postage  affixed  to  it.  Candidates  who  are  unable 
to  obtain  copies  <vf  the  prescribed  iorm  may  apply  on  any 
similar  typed  (not  handwritten)  iorm  showing  exactly  the 
wording  and  spacing  of  the  same  iorm  published  in  the 
“Calcutta  Gazette*’  of  the  1st  September  1955.  provided 
the  blanks  are  filled  tip  in  the  candidates’  own  handwriting. 

(2)  Particulars  and  certificates  required. — Candidates 
should  furnish  evidence  ol  their  age,  qualifications  and 
previous  experience  together  with  certificates  written  not 
more  than  one  your  prior  to  the  date  ol  their  applications, 
from  responsible  persons,  testifying  to  their  private 
character. 

(5)  Fee.— -Candidates  must  enclose  with  their  applica- 
tions a fee  of  Its.  5 (for  each  category  of  poets)  in  the 
form  of  a receipted  clialan  from  a Government  Treasury 
or  the  Reserve  Bank  of  India  under  the  head  “XXX VT — 
M iseellanoous  Receipts  of  the  Public  Service  Commission, 
West  Bengal”.  Money  orders,  cheques  etc.,  in  lieu  of 
treasury  ebalans  are  not  accepted.  Postal  orders, 
however,  may  be  accepted  from  candidates.  They  should 
be  crossed  and  made  payable  to  “The  Secretary,  Public 
Service  Commission,  West  Bengal”.  No  application  will 
ho  considered  unless  accompanied  with  the  requisite 
application  fee. 

Candidates  in  Government  service  should  make  sure 
before  depositing  fee  that  their  applications  will  be 
forwarded  by  their  superior  officers.  In  no  case  will  the 
fee  paid  with  the  application  be  refunded. 

The  Commission  may  remit  fee  in  case  of  genuinely 
indigent  and  bonn  fide  displaced  persons  from  Pakistan.

(3)  Fee. — Candidates  must  enclose  with  their  applica- 
tions n fee  of  Rs.  5 (for  each  category  of  poets)  in  the 
form  of  a receipted  chalan  from  a Government  Treasury 
or  the  Reserve  Bank  of  India  under  the  head  “XXXV I — 
Miscellaneous— Receipts  of  the  Public  Service  Commission, 
Went  Bengal”.  Money  orders,  cheques,  etc.,  in  lieu  Of 
treasury  chalans  are  not  accepted.  Postal  orders, 
however,  may  he  accepted  from  candidates.  They  should 
he  crossed  wnd  made  payable  to  “The  Secretary,  Public 
Service  Commission,  West  Bengal**.  No  application  will 
be  considered  unless  accompanied  with  the  requisite 
application  fee. 

Cnndidates  in  Government  service  should  make  sure 
before  depositing  fee  that  their  applications  will  be 
forwarded  by  their  superior  officers.  In  no  case  will  the 
fee  paid  with  the  application  be  refunded. 

The  Commission  may  remit  fee  in  case  of  genuinely 
indigent  and  bona  fide  displaced  persons  from  Pakistan. 

Note. — “(i)  A displaced  person  claiming  ago  concession 
must  furnish  with  his  application  satisfactory  evidence 
that  he  is  a bona  fide  displaced  person  from  Pakistan, 
e.g.,  refugee  registration  card  or  a certificate  from  a 
gazetted  officer  or  a Member  of  Parliament  or  State 
Legislature,  in  original. 

(ii)  A member  of  the  Scheduled  Caste  or  Scheduled 
Tribe  claiming  age  concession  must  furnish  with  his 
application  a certificate  in  original  from  a gazetted  officer 
or  a Member  of  Parliament  or  State  Legislature  belonging 
to  the  Scheduled  Caste  or  Scheduled  Tribe,  specifying  the 
particular  caste  or  tribe  to  which  he  claims  to  belong. 

(iii)  A displaced  person  seeking  remission  of  the 
application  fee  must  furnish  besides  the  evidence  required 
under  Note  (i)  above  a certificate  (in  original)  from  a 
District  Officer  or  a gazetted  officer  or  a Member  of 
Parliament  or  State  Legislature  to  show  that  he  is  not  in 
a position  to  pay  the  prescribed  fee.” 

(4)  Address. — Candidates  should  give  their  present 
address  and  should  communicate  at  once  any  subsequent 
change  of  address. 

(5)  Canvassing. — Any  attempt  on  the  part  of  candidates 
to  enlist  support  of  their  applications  through  persons  ot 
influence  or  officials  of  Government  will  disqualify  there 
lor  appointment.  Spontaneous  recommendations  fron 
oersons  interested  in  the  candidates  or  otherwise  known 
to  them  will  he  disregarded. 

(6)  Applications  from  candidates  who  are  in  permanent 
nr  temporary  employment  under  any  Government,  a local 
or  Statutory  Body  (e.g.,  Damodar  Valley  Corporation),  in 
India  will  be  rejected  unless  they  are  submitted  through 
i he  appointing  authority  of  their  posts  or  service. 

Candidates  serving  under  Government  or  a l°p*^ 
statutory  body  should  submit  an  advance  copy  in 
prescribed  form.  The  application  fees  should  in  sue h case 
he  attached  to  the  advance  copy  and  not  to  the  origins  ■ 
The  candidature  of  such  applicants  may  not  however 
considered  if  the  original  applications  do  not  reach  t 
Commission’s  office  within  a fortnight  from  the  cios  ^ 
date.  Unless  applications  in  original  or  advance  c»i 
with  application  fees  are  received  within  the  closing  <*» 
late  applications  may  be  rejected.

revised  working  hours  ar«  specified  below:  — 

Reading  Rooms — 

Week  days  (including  Saturdays) — 9 a m.  to  8 p.m. 

Sundays  and  holidays — 10  a.m.  to  5 p.m. 

Lending  Section — 

Week  days  (including  Saturdays) — 10  a.m.  to  6 p.m. 

Sundays  and  holidays — 10  a.m.  to  1-30  p.m. 

The  Reading  Rooms  and  the  Lending  Sections  will,  how- 
ever, remain  entirely  closed  on  the  following  days  of  tb* 
year: — 

(i)  Republic  Day,  (ii)  Independence  Day,  and  (iii) 
Mahatma  Gandhi’s  Birthday. 

Persons  above  18  years  of  age  are  elifrible  to  make  use 
of  the  Library,  which  is  a free  lending  Library  open  to 
any  one  residing  in  any  part  of  the  Indian  Union.  There 
is  no  subscription  to  pay  but  security  in  cash  is  eesenttal.

PART  II — Advertisements,  Notices 

Procedure  regarding  sending  Manuscripts  for  publication  of  Advertisements,  Notices,  etc.r  in  *>« 

“Calcutta  Gazette"  (Part  II). 

1.  Manuscripts  should  be  properly  edited  and  complete  in  itself. 

2.9$  Manuscripts  should  always  be  typewritten  on  one  side  of  the  paper.  The  name  of  the  signatory  should  be  typewritten  below  the 
signature. 

3.  Manuscripts  intended  for  advertisement  in  the  next  issue  of  “Calcutta  Gazette”  shall  be  received  by  Publication  Sales  Office  at 
New  Secretariat  Buildings,  1 Hastings  Street,  Calcutta,  up  to  3-30  p.  m.  on  Friday  and  at  Head  Office  at  Alipore  up  to  11  a.  m.  on 
Saturday. 

4.  All  costs  shall  be  paid  in  advance  and  deposited  along  with  the  manuscripts. 

5.  Manuscripts  and  postal  remittances  shall  be  addressed  to  SUPERINTENDENT,  GOVERNMENT  PRINTING  (PUBLICATION 
BRANCH),  WEST  BENGAL  GOVERNMENT  PRESS,  ALIPORE. 

The  Press  shall  not  be  held  responsible  for  delay  in  publication  of  any  advertisement  duo  to  the  non-observance  of  the  instructions 
detailed  alow.  ""

“Calcutta  Gazette”  (Part  II).

2.  Manuscripts  should  always  be  typewritten  on  one  side  of  the  paper.  The  name  of  the  signatory  should  be  typewritten  below  the 
gnature.

4.  All  costs  shall  be  paid  in  advance  and  deposited  along  with  the  manuscripts. 

5.  Manuscripts  and  postal  remittances  shall  be  addressed  to  SUPERINTENDENT,  GOVERNMENT  PRINTING  IPUBLICATION

PART  II  Advertisements,  Notices 

Procedure  regarding  sending  Manuscripts  tor  publication  of  Advertisements,  Notices,  etc.,  in  the 

“Calcutta  Gazette’*  (Part  ll>. 

1.  Manuscripts  should  be  properly  edited  and  complete  in  itself. 

2.  Manuscripts  should  always  be  typewritten  on  one  side  of  the  paper.  The  name  of  the  signatory  should  be  typewritten  below  the 
lignature. 

3 Manuscripts  intended  for  advertisement  in  the  next  issue  of  “Calcutta  Gazette”  shall  be  received  by  Publication  Sales  Office  at 
4ew  Secretariat  Buildings,  1 Hastings  Street,  Calcutta,  up  to  3-30  p.  m.  on  Friday  and  at  Head  Office  at  Alipore  up  to  11  a.  m.  on 
Saturday. 

4.  All  costs  shall  be  paid  in  advance  and  deposited  along  with  the  manuscripts. 

5 Manuscripts  and  postal  remittances  shall  be  addressed  to  SUPERINTENDENT,  GOVERNMENT  PRINTING  (PUBLICATION 
BRANCH),  WEST  BENGAL  GOVERNMENT  PRESS,  ALIPORE. 

The  Press  shall  not  be  held  responsible  for  delay  in  publication  of  any  advertisement  due  to  the  non-obaervance  of! the  instructions 
letailed  above.

PART  II  Advertisements,  Notices 

I 

rncedure  regarding  sending  Manuscripts  for  publication  of  Advertisements,  Notices,  etc.,  in  the 
roceuu  ft  * “Calcutta  Gazette”  (Part  II). 

1.  Manuscripts  should  be  properly  edited  and  complete  in  itself. 

2 Manuscripts  should  always  be  typewritten  on  one  side  of  the  paper.  The  name  of  the  signatory  should  be  typewritten  below  the 

• nature. 

3 Manuscripts  intended  for  advertisement  in  the  next  issue  of  "Calcutta  Gazette”  shall  be  received  by  Publication  Sales  Ofhcc  at 
iw  Secretariat  Buildings,  1 Hastings  Street,  Calcutta,  up  to  3-30  p.  m.  on  Friday  and  at  Head  Office  at  Alipore  up  to  11  a.  m.  on 

turday. 

4.  All  costs  shall  be  paid  in  advance  and  deposited  along  with  the  manuscripts. 

Manuscripts  and  postal  remittances  shall  be  addressed  to  SUPERINTENDENT,  GOVERNMENT  PRINTING  (PUBLICATION 
IANCH},  WEST  BENGAL  GOVERNMENT  PRESS,  ALIPORE. 

The  Press  shall  not  be  held  responsible  for  delay  in  publication  of  any  advertisement  due  to  the  non-observance  ofjthe  instruction* 

tailed  above.

national  Library 

IN  response  to  public  opinion,  the  working  hours  of  the 
Heading  (looms  and  the  Lending  Section  at  Belvedere  hare 
been  extended  with  effect  from  the  16th  August  1963.  The 
revised  working  hours  ar«  specified  below:  — 

Heading  Rooms — 

Week  days  (including  Saturdays) — 9 a.m.  to  8 p.m. 
Sundays  sold  holidays — 10  a.m.  to  6 p.m. 

Lending  Section — 

Week  days  (including  Saturdays) — 10  a.m.  to  6 p.m. 
Sundays  and  holidays — 10  a.m.  to  1-33  p.m. 

The  Reading  Rooms  and  the  Lending  Sections  will,  bow- 
over,  remain  entirely  closed  on  the  following  days  of  the 
year:  — 

(i)  Republic  Day,  (ii)  Independence  Day,  and  (iii) 
Mahatma  Gandhi's  Birthday. 

Persons  above  18  years  of  age  are  eligible  to  make  use 
of  the  Library,  which  is  a free  lending  Library  open  to 
any  one  residing  in  any  part  of  the  Indian  Union.  There 
is  no  subscription  to  pay  but  security  in  cash  is  essential.

ARTICLE  VI 

Status,  Immunities  and  Priviekoes 
Section  I.  purposes  of  Article 

To  enable  the  Corporation  to  fulfill  the  functions  with 
which  it  is  entrusted,  the  status,  immunities  and  privileges 
set  forth  in  this  Article  shall  be  accorded  to  Hie  Corporation 
in  the  territories  of  each  member. 

Section  2.  Status  of  the  Corporation 

The  Corporation  shall  possess  full  juridical  personality 
and,  in  particular,  the  capacity: 

(ij  to  contract; 

(ii)  to  acquire  and  dispose  of  immovable  and  movable 
property ; 

(iii)  to  institute  legal  proceedings. 


„T  V]  THE  CALCUTTA  GAZETTE,  JANUARY  1,  1959 


Section  3.  Position  of  the  ( 'urporation  ivith  regard  to 

J udicial  Process 

Actions  may  lie  brought  against  the  Corporation  only  in 
a court  of  competent  jurisdiction  in  the  territories  of  a 
member  in  which  the  Corporation  has  an  office,  has  appointed 
an  agent  for  the  purpose  of  accepting*  service  or  notice  of 
process,  or  has  issued  or  guaranteed  securities.  No  actions 
shall,  however,  lie  brought  liy  members  or  persons  acting* 
for  or  driving  claims  from  members.  The  property  and 
assets  of  the  Corporation  shall,  wheresoever  located  and  by 
whomsoever  held,  be  immune  from  all  forms  of  seizure, 
attachment  or  execution  before  the  delivery  of  final  jn  (Ik- 
ment  against  the  Corporation. 

Section  4.  Immunity  of  Assets  from  Seizure 

Property  and  assets  of  the  Corporation,  wherever  located 
and  by  whomsoever  held,  shall  be  immune  from  search, 
requisition,  confiscation,  expropriation  or  any  other  form  of 
seizure  by  executive  or  legislative  action. 

Section  5.  /mm  unity  of  Are  hi  res 

The  archives  of  the  Corporation  shall  be  inviolable. 

Section  (i.  Freedom  of  Assets  from  Restrictions 

To  the  extent  necessary  to  carry  out  the  operations  pro- 
vided for  in  this  Agreement  and  subject  to  the  provisions  of 
Article  IIT,  Section  5,  and  the*  other  provisions  of  this  Agree- 
ment, all  property  and  assets  of  the  Corporation  shall  be 
free  from  restrictions,  regulations,  controls  and  moratoria  of 
any  nature. 

Section  7.  Privilege  for  Corrnnvmcations 

The  official  communications  of  the  Corporation  shall  be 
accorded  by  each  member  the  same  treatment  that  it  accords 
to  the  official  communications  of  other  members. 

Section  8.  Immunities  and  Prim  leges  of  Officers  and 

Employees 

All  Governors,  Directors,  Alternate's,  officers  and 
employees  of  the  Corporation  : 

(i)  shall  be  immune  from  legal  process  with  respect  to 
acts  performed  by  them  in  their  official  capacity; 

(ii)  not  being  local  nationals,  shall  be  accorded  the 
same  immunities  from  immigration  restrict  ions, 
alien  registration  requirements  and  national 
service  obligations  and  the  same  facilities  as 
regards  exchange  restrictions  as  are  accorded  liy 
members  to  the  representatives,  officials,  and 
employees  of  compatible  rank  of  other  members; 

(Hi)  shall  be  granted  the  same  treatment  in  respect  of 
travelling  facilities  os  is  i ccorded  by  members 
to  representatives,  officials  and  employees  of  com- 
parable rank  of  other  members.

3*  All  ancient  and  historical  monuments  and  all 
archaeological  sites  and  remains  which  have  been  declared 
by  the  Ancient  and  Historical  Monuments  and  Archaeo-

of  Ijjjjl*  Importance)  Act,  1951,  or  by  section  126  of  the  States 
of  195  . Heorgan i sa tion  Ac  t,  1950,  to  be  of  national  importance  shall 
be  deemed  to  be  ancient  and  historical  monuments  or 
archieological  sites  and  remains  declared  to  be  of  national 
importance  for  the  purposes  of  this  Act. 

4.  ( 1 ) Where  the  Central  Government  is  of  opinion 

that  any  ancient  monument  or  archaeological  site  and 
remains  not  included  in  section  3 is  of  national  importance, 
it  may,  by  notification  in  the  Official  Gazette,  give  two 
months’  notice  of  its  intention  to  declare  such  ancient 
monument  or  archaeological  site  and  remains  to  be  of 
national  importance;  and  a copy  of  every  such  notification 
shall  be  affixed  in  a conspicuous  place  near  the  monument 
or  site  and  remains,  as  the  case  may  be. 

(2)  Any  person  interested  in  any  such  ancient  mounment 
or  archieological  site  and  remains  may,  within  two  months 
after  the  issue  of  the  notification,  object  to  the  declaration 
of  the  monument,  or  the  arclueological  site  and  remains,  to 
be  of  of  national  importance. 

(3)  On  the  expiry  of  the  said  period  of  two  months,  the 
Central  Government  may,  after  considering  the  objections, 
if  any,  received  by  it,  declare  by  notification  in  the  Official 
Gazette,  the  ancient  monument  or  the  archaeological  site 
and  remains,  as  the  ease  may  be,  to  be  of  national 
importance. 

(4)  A notification  published  under  sub-section  (3)  shall, 
unless  and  until  it  is  withdrawn,  be  conclusive  evidence  of 
the  fact  that  the  ancient  monument  or  the  archieological 
site  and  remains  to  which  it  relates  is  of  national  importance 
for  the  purposes  of  this  Act.

A‘*t , which  contains  a list  of  occupational  diseases,  is  proposed  to  he 
amended  and  enlarged  with  the  result  that  compensation  will  he  payable 
ih  j es peel  of  the  new  diseases  being  included  in  that  Schedule.  The  above 
proposals  will  thus  involve  increased  expenditure  from  the  Consolidated 
Fund  of  India  in  so  far  as  they  concern  the  Central  Government  under- 
takings. As  compensation  becomes  payable  only  in  the  event  of  an  employ- 
ment injury  resulting  in  disablement  or  death,  it  is  not  possible  to  estimate 
the  amount  of  increased  expenditure.

STATEMENT  OF  OBJECTS  AND  REASONS 

a\s  a result  of  t.lie  experience  gained  in  the  working  of  the  Cinemato- 
graph Act,  1952,  for  the  last  six  years,  it  is  considered  necessary  to  make 
certain  changes  in  its  provisions  for  clarification,  without  making  any 
substantial  change  in  the  working  of  the  present  Act. 

Section  3 of  the  Cinematograph  Act , 1952,  empowers  the  Central 

( lovernment  to  constitute  a Hoard  of  Film  Censors  consisting  of  such 
number  ot  persons  as  may  be  prescribed  for  the  purpose  of  examining  ami 
certifying  films  as  suitable  for  public  exhibition.  The  films  are  examined 
hy  the  regional  officers  with  the  aid  of  the  advisory  panels  consist  ng 
n't  non-officials.  The  composition  of  the  Hoard,  the  constitution  of 
the  advisory  panels  and  the  procedure  for  examination  of  films  by  tic 
regional  officer-  with  the  aid  of  the  advisoiy  panels  are  at  present  laid 
flown  in  the  Rules.  The  Hill  makes  express  provisions  in  this  behalf  in 
the  principal  Act.  It  also  incorporates  the  principles  for  guidance  in 
certifying  films,  based  cm  the  provisions  of  article  19(2^  of  the  Constitu- 
tion. In  addition,  the  Hill  makes  provision  for  certain  matter-  of  a 
procedural  and  routine  character

sanctioning  filniis  for  public*  exhibition.  As  at  present  the  Chairman  will

STATEMENT  OF  OBJECTS  AND  K EASONS 

The  Bill  is  largely  based  on  the  recommendations  ot  the  Ad\isory 
Uoanl  appointed  by  the  Government  ot  India  in  EE>‘>  to  suggest  amend- 

to  the  Indian  Electricity  Act,  1 01 0 (hereinafter  roi erred  to  as  the 
Art).  In  making  these  reeoinmendaiions,  the  Board  had,  besides  consult- 
ing ihe  State  Governments,  given  careful  eonsidei  at  ion  to  the  views  ot  the 
;>i  \ Me  sector  of  the  electricity  supply  industry. 

The  main  objects  of  the  Bill  are:-  - 

( a ) to  enlarge  the  -cope  ot  facilities  a\ailable  to  consumers  oi 
clem  l icit  y ;

private  licensees  and  State  Electricity  Boards; 

< ) to  exercise  stridor  control  over  licensees; 

d>  to  lake  powers  to  regulate  the  distribution,  supply,  consumption 

and  use  ot  energy  in  certain  ci re utnsi  a nee-  ; and 

• - to  provide  tor  the  inspection  ot  electric  works  and  installations  of 
the  (Vntral  Government.

paragraph  T of  the  Sixth  Schedule  to  the  Electricity  (Supply)  Act,  JIMS.

the  licensee  with  any  directions  issued  under  new  section  22A.  1 li<J 

clause  further  provides  for  giving  an  opportunity  to  the  licensee  of  hem  if

SUPPLEMENT  TO  THE  CALCUTTA  GAZETTE,  JANUARY  1,  1959 


CORPORATION  OF  CALCUTTA 

NOTICE 

Calcutta,  the  20th  December  1958. 

If  is  .hereby  for  general  information  that  the  Corporation  of 

Calcutta  in  exercise  of  the  powers  vested  in  it  under  section  35G  of  the  Calcutta 
Municipal  Act,  1951,  read  with  section  303  of  the  said  Act,  has,  by  its 
resolution,  dated  the  21st  November  1958,  prescribed  a 40-foot  alignment 
m continuation  of  Asoko  Road  to  meet  Alipore  Road  affecting  a portion  of 
premises  No.  14,  Asoke  Road  as  shown  in  the  plan  in  blue  dotted  lines  in 
ward  No.  72(01d  24). 

A copy  of  the  plan  prepared  in  this  behalf  may  be  seen  in  the  office  of 
the  Chief  Valuer  and  Surveyor  of  the  Corporation  on  any  working  day 
between  11  si.m.  and  2 p.m.  on  payment  of  usual  fees. 


P.  C.  MAJUMDAR, 
Chief  Executive  Officer. 


Printed  t.nd  published  bv  the  Superintendent.  Government  Printing,  West  Bengal, 
at  the' West  Bengal  Government  Press,  Alipore.

It  is  hereby  notified  for  general  information  that  the  Corporation  o 
Calcutta  in  exercise  of  the  powers  vested  in  it  under  section  356  of  tin 
Calcutta  Municipal  Act,  1951,  lias  by  its  resolution,  dated  the  19th  Septeia 
her  1958,  prescribed  the  alignment  of  JJurga  Cliaran  Doctor  Road  (portioi 
running  east  to  west  from  Lower  Circular  Road  only)  to  a width  80  ft.  1t 
modification  of  the  Corporation  resolution,  dated  the  18th  July  195(i 
Ward  No.  50.

NOTICE 

Central  Municipal  Office,  the  9th  February  1959. 

In  compliance  with  the  provisions  of  sub-section  ((>)  of  section  59  of 
the  Calcutta  Municipal  Act,  1951  (West  lien  gal  Act  XXXI  IT  of  1951),  it

Bhusan  Paul  have  been  declared  duly  elected  as  Councillors  of  the  Corpo- 
ration of  Calcutta  for  the  Constituencies  Nos.  70  and  75,  respectively.

CORPORATION  OF  CALCUTTA 


NOTICE 

Calcutta,  the  4th  February  1950. 

It  is  hereby  notified  tor  general  information  that  the  Corporation  of 
Calcutta  in  exercise  of  the  powers  vested  in  it  under  section  356  of  the 
Calcutta  Municipal  Act,  1951,  has  by  its  resolution,  dated  the  16th  January 
1959,  proscribed  a 12-ft.  alignment  connecting  16  ft.  and  20  ft.  public,  roads 
oil  For  a Hoad  and  12  ft.  public  road  off  Kankulia  Road  following  a partly 
filled  up  public  drain  in  Ward  No.  61. 

A copy  of  tho  plan  prepared  in  this  behalf  may  be  seen  in  the  office  cf 
the  Chief  Valuer  and  Surveyor  of  the  Corporation  on  any  working  day 
between  11  a.m.  and  2 p.m.  on  payment  of  usual  fees. 


P.  C.  MAJUMDAR,  Chief  Executive  Officer,

Note. — The  estimates  of  area  and  yield  of  Autumn 
Rice  for  last  year  have  been  taken  from  last 
year’s  final  forecast  based  on  the  results  of 
sample  survey  and  crop  cutting  experiments 
carried  out  by  the  State  Statistical  Bureau, 
West  Bengal.  The  figures  of  acreages 
this  year  shown  in  this  forecast  are  the  pre- 
liminary estimates  of  the  State  Statistical 
Bureau,  West.  Bengal,  based  on  sample  sui- 
vey.  The  figures  of  yield  rates  this  year  are 
however  based  on  the  eye-estimates  of  the 
extension  staff  of  this  Directorate.) 

Season. — The  weather  conditions  have  not 
generally  been  favourable  at  the  sowing  time  in 


all  the  districts  of  West  Bengal  excepting 
Murshidabad.  dalpaiguri,  Darjeeling,  West 
Dinajpur  and  Oooch  Behar.  Reports  of  attack  of 
insect  pests  have  been  received  from  the  districts 
of  Nadia,  Murshidabad,  Jalpaiguri,  Maid  a,  Wiest 
Dinajpur  and  Cooch  Behar. 

Area  and  yield. — 1,262,700  acres  have  Ibeen  esti- 
mated to  be  under  Autumn  Rice  this  year  as 
against  1,349,500  acres  estimated  for  both  the 
preliminary  and  final  forecasts  of  last  yea r. 

The  total  outturn  of  the  crop  for  the  State  as  a 
whole  in  terms  of  cleaned  rice  is  estimated  at 
317,000  tons  this  year  as  against  410,900  tons  and 
404,200  tons  estimated  respectively  for  the 
corresponding  and  final  forecasts  of  last  year. 

The  average  yield  rate  of  cleaned  rice  per  acre 
for  the  State  as  a whole  is  estimated  at  6.83 
ruaunds  this  year  as  against  8.29  maunds  and  8.15 
mauuds  estimated  for  the  corresponding  and  final 
forecasts  of  last  year.

CORPORATION  OF  CALCUTTA 

NOTICE 

Calcutta,  flic  6th  April  1959 

Notice  is  hereby'  given  for  general  information 
of  the  public  that  the  Corporation  of  Calcutta 
under  powers  vested  unto  them  under  section  361 
of  the  Calcutta  Municipal  Act,  1951 , have 
considered  it  expedient  to  sanction  the  widening 
of  the  existing  narrow  passage  between  premises 
Nos.  7,  10  and  10/1,  Burtola  Street  (Constituency 
No.  24)  to  a width  of  12  feet  as  marked  in  blue 
lines  on  the  plan  prepared  in  this  behalf. 

Copy  of  plan  prepared  in  this  behalf  may  be 
seen  in  the  office  of  the  Chief  Valuer  and  Surveyor, 
Coj-poration  of  Calcutta,  between  11  a.m.  and  2 p.m. 
on  payment  of  usual  fees. 

P.  C.  MAJUMDAfi, 

Chief  Executive  Officer.

Dated  Calcutta,  the  2nd  May  1909 

Notice  is  hereby  given  under  section  47(3)  of 
the  Calcutta  Improvement  Act,  1911  (as  amended), 
that,  the  Board  of  Trustees  for  the  Improvement  of 
Calcutta  have  applied  to  the  Local  Government  tor 
sanction  to  the  Improvement  Scheme  No.  V I F 1 — 
Maniktala  (Ultadanga  Main  Road  widening)  which 
was  first  published  in  the  ('air  alt  a (gazette  and  m 
local  newspapers  on  13th  January  L955. 

S.  K.  GUPTA, 

Chairman.
